Quadrivus strolled with some reluctance into the Temple of Roxarrum, his last visit here had been somewhat, unsatisfactory. Just as disappointing was the lack of results, there has been no news of Iskandar recently, and the great anvil in the temple remained unused. As a result, the Temple was oddly quiet, subdued, almost silent.

Deep into the Temple he went, towards the residence of Iskandar. Welcome or not, he would have to intrude. Phaedrus never asks for favours, when he does you know he's onto something big. Phaedrus had been very convincing, almost too convincing for someone uninitiated to the Order of Flux. If he was correct, then this might snap Iskandar out of his isolation.

He knocked on the door, then decided to just push it open. As expected, Iskandar had not risen to let him in. Reports show that Iskandar had been bedridden as of late, due to no physical inability, but rather out of a lack of resolve.

*"Hello Iskandar."* Quadrivus began,

"Go away. Come to make me feel worse?" Iskandar replied, a cold edge in his voice.

If Quadrivus had eyes, he would roll them.

*"As it is, no I have not come to hear your child-like complaints. Despite this, this conversation will likely consist mostly of comments that achieve that purpose. No, I have a request."*

"I am in no condition to work, is this not obvious?"

*"To the contrary. Your physical condition is impeccable. Your mental condition is poor, rather unfortunately. It is evidently holding you back. I guess I should mention, Lord Cruxius sends his best. He is unusually interested in your affairs, it seems he might have high hopes for you. I'm not here to belittle you though, I'm here because I need your help."*

"I have no reason to help you."

*"Surely you have heard of recent occurrences? Kureta is under attack."* Iskandar flinched. *"Dozens of Flora have been lost, Flora that you sacrificed so much to protect. I need your help to save them, a very small favour, nothing more."*

Iskandar sat up from his bed. "You lie."

*"Why would I come here if this were not urgent. We require your assistance, or the sacrifices that we made in their defense will be for naught."*

"What do you need?"

Quadrivus retrieved a small disk and a shaped pattern of wires. *"We need you to press this pattern into this disk. Both of these are metallic."*

"A task so trivial? Why can't you get a lesser smith to do it?"

*"Every attempt has destroyed the pattern, you're our last hope."*

"Alright, just one second."

Iskandar threw on a cloak [](#s "(Cloaks are a very common fashion accessory in Sentenza)") and led Quadrivus towards the forges. As he entered the great hall, many a Holnareem smith halted in their work in amazement, and some gathered to witness the forgemaster go to his work.

"Well, lets get on with it."

Iskandar lifted the Mutriqat Alttakwin, and took the disk that Quadrivus offered him. Then, with a deliberate motion, swung without thinking of speed. It was not too fast, nor too slow, but the precisely right, rhythmic timing that came from his experience.

As the hammer struck the disk, a wave of moonfire shot outwards, softening the disk just a bit. Then another hit, and then another, until the wafer was the right size for the array.

Quadrivus carefully gave Iskandar the delicate pattern, and in between the strikes, Iskandar swiftly placed the pattern onto the disk.

With one more great strike, the two fused, and the pattern was forced into the disk. Iskandar waited for the disk to cool, then handed it to Quadrivus.

Quadrivus waved his hand, and suddenly the air above the disk began to glow rather strongly. He let out a feeling of satisfaction.

*"Wonderful work Iskandar, truly marvelous."*

The watching smiths, transfixed by the work, applauded, then seeing Iskandar's annoyance returned to their work.

"Is that it? What does this do?"

*"I don't know, you would have to ask Phaedrus, he merely said this is very important. It is nice to see such skilled workmanship, you see what impact your return has had on the smiths?"*

Iskandar looked around, the smiths were working as if elated, many were working with an extraordinary vigour, as if inspired by what they just saw.

*"They need you Iskandar, you belong here."*

Iskandar looked at the hammer, perfectly fitting in his hand. It just felt right to be wielding it again.

*"I guess you'll understand, we'll be needing more of these disks."*

Iskandar considered for a second. Perhaps he was fleshchanged, but first and foremost he was a smith, forgemaster of the Temple. This was what he devoted his life towards, this was a calling, much more real and palpable than a fleshchanged nature.

With an iron resolve, Iskandar grinned and replied.

"When do we begin?"
